claimed_purpose.text: The first benchmark for multimodal, multi-source personalized referential memory QA over long time horizons (~4 years), with evidence-grounded retrieval and answering.

mechanisms.text: Five named ability dimensions tested: personalized reference resolution (PR), location awareness (LA), memory updates over time (MUT), multi-evidence composition (ME), and abstention (ABS)
Raw modality degrades under haystack conditions and can fail due to model image/video count or API payload limits; SGM is preferred representation for realistic noisy conditions.
NIAH (Needle-in-a-Haystack style) evaluation uses generation-only mode with fixed evidence pools, tested across two model families and two memory representations (SGM and raw).
Evidence is multimodal (images, videos, emails). Text-only mode uses precomputed batch_results.json (captions/OCR/tags); raw mode inserts actual images/videos into the prompt.
Each question in the dataset carries ground-truth evidence IDs. The Oracle baseline uses these IDs directly to test answer synthesis quality given perfect retrieval.
A two-stage memory/answerer model architecture is canonical: a smaller model (2B) handles ingestion/indexing and a larger model (8B) handles QA.
Two canonical QA data files exist: atm-bench.json (standard split) and atm-bench-hard.json (hard split), both located under data/atm-bench/.
SGM schema fields are modality-aware: image/video fields are time, location, entities, ocr, tags; email fields are time, summary, body.
Primary metric is QS (Query Score, reported as accuracy percentage). Recall@10 is also reported for memory-system baselines.
Primary judge for QS score is gpt-5-mini; some rows use a DeepSeek-V4-flash judge, which is flagged with an asterisk.
Memory ingestion is chronological: emails, images, and videos are merged and sorted by timestamp before ingestion.
The SGM text representation for media uses fields: type, timestamp, location, short_caption, caption, ocr, tags.
NIAH results can be summarized into a Markdown table using a dedicated script with configurable output root.
Input modalities include images, videos, and emails spanning approximately 4 years of personal memory.
Scale: approximately 12k memory items, approximately 1.1k QA pairs, years-long horizon
Dataset is human-curated with evidence labels, not synthetic

ledger.quote: The first benchmark for multimodal, multi-source personalized referential memory QA over long time horizons (~4 years), with evidence-grounded retrieval and answering.

ledger.quote: run any Harbor agent against the 31 hard questions in per-question Docker isolation

ledger.quote: ATM-Bench QS ↑ | ATM-Bench Recall@10 ↑ | ATM-Bench-Hard QS ↑ | ATM-Bench-Hard Recall@10 ↑

ledger.locator: README.md, Oracle and NIAH Results section

ledger.quote: Multimodal and multi-source data: Images, videos, emails ... Long-term horizon: ~4 years of personal memory
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: Full dataset download is approximately 3.3 GB.
ledger.quote: Full download (~3.3 GB) — includes QA, NIAH pools, preprocessed memory, emails, raw images, raw videos, and the GPS reverse-geocoding cache

ledger.claim: Metric definitions and full grader specification are deferred to docs/metrics.md; only metric names and judge model are stated in README.
ledger.quote: `docs/metrics.md` - Evaluation metrics
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: SGM representation is recommended over Raw for realistic/agentic evaluation because Raw degrades and fails under haystack conditions.
ledger.quote: Raw outperforms SGM at the Oracle ceiling. But that advantage collapses under realistic conditions: as the haystack fills with distractors, raw degrades and even fails (payload/context limits), and under agentic retrieval the gap is stark — every 'w/o SGM' (raw) agent lands far below its SGM run.
ledger.locator: README.md, Oracle and NIAH Results, Why SGM callout
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Harness and model are treated as one system, not independent factors, because the same model can differ by several points across harnesses.
ledger.quote: The same model can differ by several points across harnesses — GLM-5.2 scores 47.7% under Claude Code and 45.1% under Pi, Kimi K2.7 Code 47.0% / 39.2% / 37.8% under Claude Code, Pi and OpenCode. Harness and model are one system here, not two independent factors.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: ATMBench is an evidence-grounded benchmark; models are prompted to answer only from retrieved evidence and return Unknown when evidence is insufficient.
ledger.quote: ATMBench is an evidence-grounded benchmark. Most baselines use prompts that: instruct the model to answer only from retrieved evidence, and return Unknown when evidence is insufficient.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The standard QA input file is data/atm-bench/atm-bench.json and the hard split is data/atm-bench/atm-bench-hard.json.
ledger.quote: QA files: data/atm-bench/atm-bench.json / data/atm-bench/atm-bench-hard.json
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Evidence modalities include images, videos, and emails. Text-only mode uses batch_results.json (captions/OCR/tags); raw mode passes actual media into the prompt.
ledger.quote: --media-source batch_results: treat images/videos as text via precomputed batch_results.json (captions/OCR/tags). --media-source raw: load raw images/videos and insert them into the prompt (multimodal inference).
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §Baseline Principles / Text-only vs raw-media modes
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The Oracle baseline uses ground-truth evidence IDs from the dataset, measuring answer synthesis quality given perfect retrieval, not retrieval quality.
ledger.quote: An upper bound baseline that uses ground-truth evidence IDs from the dataset and asks the model to answer. What it measures: Answer synthesis quality given perfect retrieval (not a retrieval baseline).
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §Oracle / What it is / What it measures
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Oracle baseline is implemented in memqa/qa_agent_baselines/oracle/oracle_baseline.py.
ledger.quote: Implementation: memqa/qa_agent_baselines/oracle/oracle_baseline.py
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: NIAH is a generation-only protocol on the hard split; each question has a niah_evidence_ids field with a fixed pool guaranteed to contain the ground truth. The evaluator swaps this into evidence_ids and calls oracle_baseline.py.
ledger.quote: A generation-only protocol for the hard split where each question includes a fixed evidence pool (niah_evidence_ids) guaranteed to contain the ground truth. niah_evaluate.py is a wrapper around the Oracle baseline: it swaps niah_evidence_ids -> evidence_ids and then calls oracle_baseline.py.
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §NIAH / What it is / How it is implemented here
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The SGM text representation for media evidence uses fields: type, timestamp, location, short_caption, caption, ocr, tags.
ledger.quote: The *_SGM.sh scripts use --media-source batch_results with the paper's SGM fields: type,timestamp,location,short_caption,caption,ocr,tags.
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §NIAH / How it is implemented here
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval recall outputs (retrieval_recall_details.json, retrieval_recall_summary.json) are produced by baselines including MMRAG, HippoRAG2, MemoryOS, A-Mem, Mem0, and MemPalace.
ledger.quote: <output>/retrieval_recall_details.json / <output>/retrieval_recall_summary.json
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: MemPalace computes R@{1,5,10,25,50,100} by over-fetching 100 candidates and persisting the ranked list; only top --retrieve-k (default 10) go to the answerer.
ledger.quote: --n-results defaults to 100 (upstream default is 5). The full ranked list is persisted in retrieval_recall_details.json so R@{1,5,10,25,50,100} can be computed; only the top --retrieve-k (default 10) items are passed to the answerer.
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §MemPalace / Key design choices / Over-fetch for recall reporting
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: MemPalace outputs include retrieval_recall_joint_accuracy_summary.json, indicating joint retrieval-and-answer accuracy is tracked.
ledger.quote: <output>/retrieval_recall_joint_accuracy_summary.json
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Evaluation contamination is explicitly mitigated: per-question isolation via checkpoint restore and/or no-update mode (skip post-answer writes) are implemented where applicable.
ledger.quote: Where applicable we implement: per-question isolation (fresh instance restored from a checkpoint), and/or no-update evaluation mode (skip post-answer writes).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: MemoryOS full-history mode is the canonical benchmark setting, enforcing floors on MTM capacity (>=20000) and session search depth (>=200) and suppressing promotion churn (heat_threshold>=1e9).
ledger.quote: Full-history variant (this repo's benchmark setting): memoryos_mid_term_capacity >= 20000 / memoryos_top_k_sessions >= 200 / memoryos_heat_threshold >= 1e9 (suppresses MTM→LPM promotion churn)
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §MemoryOS / Paper defaults vs full-history variant
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory ingestion merges emails, images, and videos sorted by timestamp before ingestion into memory systems.
ledger.quote: We merge emails/images/videos and sort by timestamp before ingestion.
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §MemoryOS / Key design choices / Chronological indexing
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Canonical default model sizes are 2B for memory/indexing and 8B for answering across multiple baselines.
ledger.quote: In this repo's canonical run scripts, the defaults follow: 2B model for memory/indexing / 8B model for answering.
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §Baseline Principles / Memory/index model vs answerer model
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: GPS/reverse-geocoding of media is performed via OpenStreetMap Nominatim; a local geocoding cache keyed by media filename stem can be pre-populated to skip rate-limited calls.
ledger.quote: By default, the processors reverse-geocode GPS coordinates via a public provider (OpenStreetMap Nominatim). Public geocoding endpoints are rate-limited... GPS cache files are keyed by the media filename stem.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: mem0's LLM-based extraction pipeline often returns empty facts for structured batch-result items; the canonical script defaults to direct embedding storage (--no-mem0-infer).
ledger.quote: mem0 supports an LLM-based extraction/update pipeline (--mem0-infer) that is optimized for conversational personal facts. For structured batch-result style items, the upstream extraction prompt often returns empty facts, producing a near-empty index. Therefore, the canonical script defaults to: MEM0_INFER=0 → --no-mem0-infer
ledger.locator: docs/baseline.md §Mem0 / Important note about mem0 extraction
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: ATM-Bench has two difficulty splits: a standard split and a hard split (ATM-bench-hard), both exercised by the MMRAG pipeline.
